key_insight: Crystal prototype reuse supports materials discovery, but family definitions and training coverage strongly influence apparent prediction success and novelty.
engineering_relevance: Prototype libraries can guide substitution, screening, and crystal structure prediction when structural equivalence rules match the engineering task.
method: Survey curated and automated prototype libraries and their classification algorithms.
Analyze GraphID family coverage and neighbor-tolerance sensitivity across four materials databases.
Compare 12 generative crystal structure prediction models and test reduced-stoichiometry holdouts.
evidence_signal: Across analyzed database samples, the top 100 families cover 30–67% of structures; template retrieval achieves the highest top-1 success rate among the 12 compared models.
watch_item: Stoichiometry-held-out failures do not establish unseen-prototype generalization; family assignments also depend strongly on neighbor tolerance.
paper_title: A Comprehensive Survey of Crystal Structural Prototypes: Construction, Classification, and Applications
